newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Low Euro gas oil stocks may cause winter problems.
newsitem.headline: Low Euro gas oil stocks may cause winter problems.

text.p: European gas oil stocks have barely grown through the summer, the traditional stock-building season, and should ensure gas oil margins remain firm in the last quarter of the year, analysts said on Tuesday.

"Overall, the stocks really are rather low compared with a year ago and it could have a significant effect, particularly if we have a cold winter," said Peter Bogin of oil consultants Cambridge Energy Research Associates.

Middle distillate stocks in the 14 countries of the European Union excluding Sweden grew by 3.75 million barrels in August to 286.28 million barrels, according to the latest monthly report from Stichting Euroilstock.
German middle distillate stocks themselves actually dropped by 2.63 million barrels in August, but analysts believe the fall may reflect a slow build by end consumers.

However, for the whole of Europe distillate stocks have risen by less than 10 million barrels, or 1.33 million tonnes, from the end of April to the end of August. The stock levels at the end of August were also 25.79 million barrels, or 8.3 percent, lower than at the end of August 1995.
"In 1994, there was a build from May to August of 3.2 million tonnes. In 1996, we have a very modest build and the stocks are incredibly low," said Cindy Poynter of oil consultants, Bonner and Moore.
Analysts say the bullish implication for gas oil margins for the remainder of the year is clear.
"Considering where the U.S. and Europe are, one can afford to be quite, quite bullish on gas oil," said Poynter.
"These figures are good news for the gas oil margin and should keep prices high," said Bogin.

The Euroil figures also highlight the steady rise of gasoline stocks and possible problems of worsening oversupply to come. At 153.51 million barrels, gasoline stocks are 1.6 percent higher than at the end of August 1995. If European refiners up their utilisation rate to increase gas oil, they will produce more unwanted gasoline.
"Europe is long gasoline and will go out of balance even more if we have a cold winter which draws down the gas oil stocks," said Poynter.
